correctness.rationale: For every r>=2,n>=r+2, point-side D_X is the (r-1)-skeleton, whose r-flagification is the full simplex. A minimal-empty-intersection argument shows all and only newly adjoined subset-side faces are the r-simplices indexed by T of size r+1. The natural good-cover nerve equivalence carries each boundary to the corresponding simplex-skeleton boundary, so simultaneous attaching produces skel_r Delta^{n-1}. An acyclic matching of this skeleton gives exactly C(n-1,r+1) r-spheres. Direct independent finite rank checks agree but are not used to prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The exact binomial-rank defect shows, for every arity r, that the guaranteed homology equivalence below r is sharp at the next degree. The failure can be unbounded even while one flagified side is contractible, giving a structural and topological boundary for using higher-flagified Dowker approximations, rather than merely one numerical counterexample.
